US-119-HR10940.title: READI Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10940.description: To direct the Federal Communications Commission to promulgate regulations establishing metrics, goals, and minimum requirements with respect to the delivery of wireless emergency alerts, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10940.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Federal Communications Commission to set rules for wireless emergency alerts, including measures for speed, reliability, and sending alerts to the right area. It would require providers that send these alerts to collect and report data, and would have the FCC publish yearly updates on whether providers meet the goals and minimum rules. It would also require a study of advanced translation tools for multi-language alerts, a possible pilot test, and clearer warnings before a user opts out of certain alerts.

US-119-HR10885.title: PROTECT Small Restaurants Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10885.description: To ensure delivery service providers have partnership agreements with the restaurants for which the providers deliver, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10885.aiSummary: The bill would require food delivery apps and other delivery services to have a written partnership agreement with a restaurant before they can take orders for that restaurant. If a restaurant asks and there is no agreement, the service would have to remove the restaurant from its online platform and stop handling its orders within 10 days. The Federal Trade Commission would enforce the rule, and it would apply to orders placed 180 days after the law takes effect. It would also make an FTC rule on impersonating government and businesses carry the force of law.

US-119-HR10863.title: Vets and Pets Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10863.description: To authorize the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out a pilot program under which the Secretary awards grants to nonprofit organizations to assist such organizations in providing dogs and cats as pets for eligible veterans, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10863.aiSummary: The bill would set up a pilot program at the Department of Veterans Affairs to give grants to nonprofit groups that provide dogs or cats to eligible veterans. Those groups would also help pay for starter supplies, spaying or neutering, and initial shots and medicine for the pets. The program would end after fiscal year 2028, and up to $1,000,000 would be available for fiscal years 2027 through 2028.

US-119-HR10841.title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10841.description: To prohibit the use of artificial intelligence to deprive or defraud individuals of the right to vote in elections for public office, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10841.aiSummary: The bill would bar people who build or use artificial intelligence from using it to trick, threaten, or stop people from voting in federal, state, or local elections. It would also require clear labels on certain AI-made election content, like altered images, fake voice clips, or voting info, and the Federal Trade Commission would enforce these rules. It would apply to developers and users of these systems, and some parts would take effect 60 days after enactment or 60 days after the FTC issues rules.

US-119-HR10786.title: Civic Literacy in Higher Education Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10786.description: To amend the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require certain institutions to require students who are United States citizens to pass the United States naturalization test in order to graduate, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10786.aiSummary: The bill would change federal higher education rules so some colleges and universities would have to make U.S. citizen students pass the U.S. naturalization test before graduating. The test would have to be given by a faculty member, with no books or notes. It would apply to certain institutions covered by the Higher Education Act.

US-119-HR10764.title: Executive Settlement Review Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10764.description: To amend title 31, United States Code, to require certain procedures for compromise settlements or awards for executive branch officials, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10764.aiSummary: The bill would set special court steps for certain settlements or awards for some executive branch people and related entities. For claims of $250,000 or more, or for nonmoney relief, the case would go to a three-judge federal court in Washington, D.C., and any appeal would go to the D.C. Circuit court. The settlement proposal would have to be filed, published, open for public comment, and reviewed by the court before approval.

US-119-HR10687.title: Utility Affordability and Transparency Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10687.description: To modify the emergency authority under section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act to increase transparency for ratepayers and prohibit orders that prevent or delay the retirement of power plants.
US-119-HR10687.aiSummary: The bill would change how the Energy Secretary can use emergency power orders under the Federal Power Act. It would require more public explanation and reporting about why an order is issued, its expected costs, and its effects on utilities and customers. It would also bar orders that stop or delay a power plant from retiring, unless a special emergency is met and the grid operator asks for that delay in writing.

US-119-HR10621.title: Medicaid Fraud Fighting and Taxpayer Protection Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10621.description: To amend title XIX of the Social Security Act to increase the State share of recovery under laws relating to false or fraudulent claims under the Medicaid program.
US-119-HR10621.aiSummary: The bill would raise the state share of money recovered in Medicaid fraud cases from 10 percentage points to 25 percentage points. It would affect states that bring actions under Medicaid false-claim rules. The change would apply to amounts recovered in state actions brought on or after the date the law is enacted.

US-119-S603.title: A bill to designate the General George C. Marshall House, in the Commonwealth of Virginia, as an affiliated area of the National Park System, and for other purposes.
US-119-S603.summary:
This bill establishes the General George C. Marshall House in Leesburg, Virginia, as an affiliated area of the National Park System to promote public appreciation of the historic contributions made by George Catlett Marshall, Jr. (George Catlett Marshall, Jr. served as Army Chief of Staff during World War II, and later as Secretary of State, president of the American Red Cross, and Secretary of Defense.)

The bill designates the George C. Marshall International Center as the management entity for the affiliated area. The Department of the Interior must enter into an agreement with the center that describes the roles and responsibilities for management of the affiliated area. Further, Interior may provide technical assistance and enter into cooperative agreements with the center for the purpose of providing financial assistance for the marketing, marking, interpretation, and preservation of the affiliated area.

US-119-HR10544.title: Ovarian Cancer IMPACT Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10544.description: To modernize and strengthen Federal efforts to improve ovarian cancer awareness, hereditary cancer risk assessment, access to genetic counseling and testing, and access to specialty care, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10544.aiSummary: The bill would expand federal efforts on ovarian cancer awareness, genetic risk checks, genetic counseling and testing, and access to specialty care. It would also require many health plans to cover certain genetic tests, early detection steps, and risk-reducing care for people at higher hereditary risk, with an effective date for those coverage rules starting 1 year after enactment. The bill also sets up grants, outreach, and reporting rules, and it authorizes $20 million each year from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for part of the program.

US-119-S5460.title: Healthy Meals Help Kids Learn Act of 2026
US-119-S5460.summary:
Healthy Meals Help Kids Learn Act of 2026

This bill permanently increases the federal reimbursement rates for the school lunch and breakfast programs.

Specifically, beginning October 1, 2026, the bill provides an additional 45 cents per lunch served in the National School Lunch Program and an additional 28 cents per breakfast served in the School Breakfast Program. These amounts must be adjusted annually for inflation beginning July 1, 2027.
US-119-S5460.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2026-09-23)

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5460.aiSummary: The bill would raise the federal payment rate for school lunches and breakfasts. Starting October 1, 2026, it would add 45 cents for each lunch served in the National School Lunch Program and 28 cents for each breakfast served in the School Breakfast Program. Those amounts would be adjusted each year for inflation starting July 1, 2027, affecting schools that serve these meals.

US-119-HR10522.title: Companion Animal Protection Against Cruel Testing Act
US-119-HR10522.summary:
Companion Animal Protection Against Cruel Testing Act

This bill prohibits the use of funds made available to covered federal agencies for any biomedical research activity involving a live dog or cat. Covered agencies are agencies or offices within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that award, administer, or expend federal funds for biomedical research.

This prohibition also applies to activities that materially facilitate biomedical research involving a live dog or cat (e.g., salaries, facility maintenance, and administrative support primarily related to such research). It does not apply to transportation and rehousing of animals previously used in biomedical research or observational activities that do not involve alteration of an animal’s normal environment or medical care.

The prohibition applies to federal funds obligated or expended beginning 180 days after the bill is enacted. HHS may waive the prohibition in limited circumstances if necessary to respond to a specified emergency.

Recipients of funding from covered agencies must make reasonable efforts to transfer dogs and cats no longer needed for research to rescue organizations or other appropriate entities. Further, recipients may only euthanize an animal if a veterinarian has determined euthanasia is necessary for animal welfare or public safety.

If HHS determines that a recipient has violated a provision of the bill, it may withhold further funding to the recipient, recover funds expended in violation, and impose other administrative remedies.

Finally, the Government Accountability Office must report to Congress on the bill's implementation within three years after the bill takes effect.
US-119-HR10522.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-09-21)

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10522.aiSummary: The bill would bar covered federal health agencies from using federal money for biomedical research on live dogs or cats. It would also cover spending that mainly supports that research, like staff pay, building upkeep, and office help. Groups that get these funds would have to try to place unneeded dogs and cats with rescue groups or others, and could euthanize them only if a vet says it is needed for the animal’s welfare or public safety. The ban would start 180 days after enactment, and HHS could allow a limited waiver in certain emergencies.

US-119-HR10324.title: ROMA Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10324.description: To amend the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 to establish a database of isotopic signatures for processing tomatoes, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10324.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Agriculture Department to create and keep a database of isotopic signatures for processing tomatoes, which are tomatoes used for paste or other processed foods. It would also support research on testing methods, and let federal agencies, schools, research stations, and private groups request the database information. The department would work with Customs and Border Protection on import checks and send Congress a report within 2 years of enactment.

US-119-HR204.title: ACRES Act
US-119-HR204.summary:
Accurately Counting Risk Elimination Solutions Act or the ACRES Act

This bill establishes requirements regarding reports about hazardous fuels reduction activities and standardized procedures for tracking data for hazardous fuels reduction. Hazardous fuels reduction activities means any vegetation management activities that reduce the risk of wildfire but excludes the award of contracts to conduct hazardous fuels reduction activities.

First, the Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the Department of the Interior must include in the materials submitted in support of the President's budget each fiscal year a report on the number of acres of federal land on which such activities were carried out during the preceding year.

Next, USDA and Interior must implement standardized procedures for tracking data related to such activities. The standardized procedures must include
• regular, standardized data reviews of the accuracy and timely input of data used to track hazardous fuels reduction activities;
• verification methods that validate whether such data accurately correlates to such activities;
• an analysis of the short- and long-term effectiveness of such activities on reducing the risk of wildfire; and
• for hazardous fuels reduction activities that occur partially within the wildland-urban interface, methods to distinguish which acres are located within and which located outside the wildland-urban interface.

Finally, the Government Accountability Office must (1) conduct a study on this bill's implementation, and (2) submit a report to Congress with the results of the study.
US-119-HR204.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-01-03)

US-119-HR9434.title: REG Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9434.description: To amend the Federal securities laws to require rulemakings to consider the cumulative effects of the rule with certain other final and proposed rules.
US-119-HR9434.aiSummary: The bill would change federal securities laws so agencies must look at the combined effect of a new rule with certain other recent rules and proposed rules. It would apply to rulemaking under the Securities Act, the Securities Exchange Act, the Investment Company Act, and the Investment Advisers Act. These changes would affect federal regulators that write securities rules.
